To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(a) the non-extractable fraction of organic xenobiotics is not negligible and that (b) it differs in qualitative and quantitative composition compared to the extractable fraction.

the non-extractable fraction of organic contaminants can be significantly larger than the extractable fraction and that the non-extracable fraction can contain a variety of compounds, some of which are not known from other environmental compartments.

the investigated sediment samples contained extractable and nonextractable organic xenobiotic compounds, which were identified as chlorinated benzenediphenylmethane derivatives, anisoles and styrenes.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development and application of new analytical techniques for the identification and quantification of extractable and, for the first time, non-extractable compounds in subaquatic sediments and with the interpretation of the analytical results with respect to the modes of incorporation and the origin of the detected anthropogenic organic compounds.
the development and application of a non-target screening method for the analysis of extractable and particularly non-extractable compounds in sediments.
the elucidation of the chemical composition of organic xenobiotics incorporated into the organic matrix of sediments, and the identification and characterization of their modes of incorporation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
non-extractable xenobiotics are ubiquitous in sediments and that the non-extractable fraction is a significant reservoir for anthropogenic compounds.
non-extractable organics are an important and often dominating fraction of anthropogenic compounds in subaquatic sediment.
the non-extractable fraction of anthropogenic organic pollutants is a significant part of the total anthropogenic burden.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the incorporation of organic xenobiotics into the organic carbon matrix of riverine sediment depends strongly on their chemical properties.
a combination of extractive and degradative techniques is a powerful tool for a comprehensive investigation of anthropogenic organic compounds in subaquatic sediment samples.
the non-extractable fraction of sedimentary organic matter is an important sink for anthropogenic organic compounds.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the analysis of non-extractable xenobiotics in sediments is feasible and that it is necessary to consider the non-extractable fraction in the assessment of the contamination status.

the non-extractable fraction is not only of importance with respect to the total amount of anthropogenic compounds present in sediments, but also in terms of the chemical composition of the non-extractables.

a comprehensive characterization of anthropogenic organic compounds in riverine sedi-ments requires the application of non-target screening approaches, which allow the detection of a broad spectrum of compounds.
